Replay. What the planner would have done in August 2026, standing on each morning with no later data. The factory did not run this way. WhatsApp replies are written in, not received.

Questions for Daman

Everything the study could not settle from data, in one place — asked 2026-08-31. Each one carries my best guess, so a one-word confirm or correction is enough. Anything I could have looked up myself was dropped rather than asked.

Blocking — changes the model

4 questions
1

Free space = ceiling minus SAP OnHand minus everything invoiced but not yet gated out — counting BOTH exit lanes (the dock for customers, and Warehouse BST for the Mart transfers). Is that the formula you meant by C-0054?

My guess
Yes — that is exactly what you described. I have built it that way and it is in out/storage-corrected-final.csv. Space is released when the vehicle leaves, and there are two vehicle-out records, not one.
blocks: Wiring the correction into the storage model. The join is built and the daily series is computed; no engine file has been changed.Gurvinderjeet Singh +91 93193 79079OPEN — mechanism confirmed, formula NOT ratified
Daman 2026-08-30: 'the analogy I explained to you was right, but I don't think I have live numbered reports. Keep that in the questions, we'll clear it later.' So: the INVOICE-FIRST-TRUCK-LATER mechanism is confirmed by the owner and by SAP (1,055 TransType-13 movements, zero TransType-15 — no delivery note exists, the invoice IS the stock movement). What is NOT ratified is whether ceiling - OnHand - invoiced-not-gated-out (both doors) is the formula JIVO wants to manage space by. No JIVO-side report shows physical occupancy today.
2

Is the basement (BH-BT) 628 pallet positions or 739? Your capacity sheet says 628. The factory app's own rack map for the basement has 739 cells tagged Finished Goods, one pallet each.

My guess
739 — the sheet is stale, probably counted before a bay was added. I verified the 739 cells live in the app tonight. Say the word and I will move the ceiling to 907,000 L.
Changed since the rebuild
The ceiling is now the least-verified number in the whole model. This decides it.
blocks: The ceiling itself, and therefore whether August was an overflow event that needs a post-mortem or just a tight month.
3

Is Gupta still available to Oil as an overflow godown, or is that door shut? The Bhakharpur-to-Gupta transfers ran 417,000-542,000 pieces every month from February to July, then stopped dead on 23 July — one day after the basement opened — and have taken nothing since.

My guess
The basement replaced Gupta on purpose and the building is going to Mart, but the door is not bricked up — Oil's own corner still holds 226,320 L today, so it could be reopened if you allow it.
blocks: The whole overflow plan — whether a tight month is a scheduling problem or a physical one.
4

Do the filling lines actually stop around 16:20, or do they keep running to about 19:00 with the output keyed in once at the end of the run?

My guess
They keep running. The 16:20-to-19:00 block is real production that nobody keys segment by segment. So the honest reading is a long day at about 47% efficiency, not a short day at 100%.
Changed since the rebuild
More important since the rebuild — v2 runs lines at 50% of rated. If they run past 16:20, that 50% means something else.
blocks: The entire capacity model, and whether the answer to a demand spike is a second shift or just better use of the day you already pay for.

High

5 questions
5

Is there a target for how long a bill may sit between the invoice and the truck? Today Oil's median is 2 days and the slowest one bill in ten waits more than 8 days, while the dock itself only takes about 2.5 hours.

My guess
There is no target today and it has been drifting better on its own (4.85 days in June, 3.95 in July, 2.22 in August). I would set 24 hours as the goal — but it may be the customer's or the transporter's timing, not ours, in which case it is not a lever.
blocks: Knowing whether the ~145,000 L average standing pile is a problem to fix or just the cost of doing business.
6

Trucks per day have never gone above 26 in seventy days, median 19. What actually caps it — number of docks, loading labour, gate hours, or transporters?

My guess
Loading labour and dock positions, not trucks. Loading takes 137 minutes a truck for Oil while the gate itself takes minutes, and arrivals all bunch at 10:00 with nothing moving between 20:00 and 08:00.
blocks: Putting a drain-rate constraint next to the 827 T ceiling. Without it the plan can assume goods leave as fast as they are made.
7

Does GP-FG — Oil's own corner of the Gupta building — belong inside the space model with its own ceiling, or does it stay outside because the building is committed to Mart?

My guess
Give it a ceiling and keep it in. It is doing real work. Note its 226,320 L includes about 203,000 L of imported soyabean tins booked as semi-finished, which an earlier count filtered out — a tin of oil takes up floor whatever group it sits in.
blocks: Giving GP-FG a ceiling, and deciding whether overflow from BH-BT/BH-PF may legitimately be planned into it.
8

Is Clear Pack really 3,000 five-litre bottles an hour? The best stretch that line has ever managed at 5 L is 2,695, and a typical run does 1,025 to 1,509.

My guess
3,000 looks like the 1 L number copied across. I would use about 1,500/hr for 5 L until you say otherwise.
Changed since the rebuild
Already acted on — v2 uses 1,000/hr for Clear Pack 5 L (observed median 831). Confirm or correct.
blocks: 5 L capacity in the month plan, and therefore whether the 5 L SKUs can be promised at all.
9

When Accounts bills ahead of the truck, does the stock get moved to a staging lane or dock-side stack, or does it stay in its rack until the truck comes?

My guess
It stays in the rack. The box scans show pallets being pulled straight from their godown cell onto the truck at loading time, not from a staging area.
blocks: Whether the fix is 'stop billing early' or 'add a staging lane'.

Medium

9 questions
10

What is BH-PF's 377,000 L ceiling actually based on, and is it right? It has no rack map and no capacity figure on file — 377,000 is your 450/502 haircut applied to the sheet's 421 T.

My guess
The ceiling is about right but it is derived, not measured. A pallet count on the first floor would settle it the same way the basement's 739 cells did.
blocks: Knowing whether last week was a near-miss worth acting on or noise.
11

Two things about the weighbridge, and they resolve together: when was it last calibrated and stamped — and should the received quantity follow OUR weighed net instead of the supplier's billed quantity?

My guess
The bridge is probably fine and the suppliers are probably short-loading slightly — the shortfall is too consistent across four different suppliers to be one scale drifting. But I would get the certificate before saying a word to anyone.
blocks: Whether to raise this with AWL, Dhanlaxmi, Vaishnodevi and Arora at all. I will not call it a loss until the calibration certificate is seen.
12

The 43.91 MT of imported pomace olive that came in on 17 August (truck RJ47GA8215, POs 220526015 and 220526016, Rs 1.00 Cr) — where is it physically now? Bhakharpur, Gujarat, or already out to job work?

My guess
In the Bhakharpur oil tanks (BH-LO) with the GRPO simply not keyed yet — the gate entry is at Bhakharpur, not Gujarat. Median gate-to-GRPO is 1 day but the tail runs to 18, and this one is stuck in the tail.
blocks: Whether to add it to available oil in the September plan, and whether someone needs to chase the GRPO.
13

Should the day plan refuse to schedule a run whose bill of materials exceeds the packaging actually on hand, or only warn? Today three of the seven runs raised were short — canola 1,644 L available against 10,000 needed, and 3,735 SANO 5 L tins against 4,000.

My guess
Warn loudly, do not refuse — the floor clearly starts runs short and finishes them, and a hard block would stop work the plant knows how to do.
Changed since the rebuild
v2 currently REFUSES to schedule short. Your answer flips it to warn-only.
blocks: Whether the day plan the engine emits is actually schedulable or just arithmetic.
14

Do you want a real hold status with an owner and an age? Today a hold is typed into the remarks box as free text — 'HOLD BY NAVNEET VG', 'BH-PS GODOWN DO NOT DISPATCH' — 41 bills in 90 days.

My guess
Yes, and it should be a field with a name and a date on it so a hold cannot quietly become permanent.
blocks: A hold queue the planner can subtract from free space.
15

Who is supposed to key the case counts into the production app during the shift, and does anyone check them? The segments add to 59,723 cases for August, the run headers say 88,139, and SAP says the plant made about 105,000.

My guess
The operator keys them and nobody checks. Use the app for TIME and SAP for VOLUME — that combination reconciles, and the two on their own do not.
blocks: Whether the factory app can ever be the production system of record, or stays a shift diary with SAP as the volume truth.
16

Would you have the dispatch team set the planned dispatch date a day or two ahead instead of on the day? The field, the priority flag and a 14-day board already exist and are empty beyond today.

My guess
Yes, and it costs nothing — one field filled a day earlier. But it may be that the truck genuinely is not known until the morning, in which case there is nothing to fill in.
blocks: Any forward space forecast. I can build the report the moment the data exists; I cannot invent the dates.
17

Do customer returns and branch stock transfers physically come through the same gate? The app has finished modules for both and neither has ever been used once, while SAP books 28 A/R returns, 6 vendor returns and 444 stock transfers in Oil in August alone.

My guess
Same gate, recorded as an ordinary vehicle entry with no returns paperwork behind it. The volumes are small next to dispatch, so I would not chase it before the outbound side is fixed.
blocks: Whether the free-space model needs an inbound-returns term as well as the outbound one.
18

Is the crude-out / cold-press-back job-work loop through BH-GJ weighed and recorded anywhere? The gate's job-work module has 14 records and every one has an empty SAP document, empty production order and empty item list.

My guess
It is weighed at the job worker's end and comes back to us as a GRPO quantity we do not independently check. That is why the 3% refining loss can only be inferred from ratios, never measured.
blocks: Closing the oil material balance.

Low

4 questions
19

Mart inbound never touches the gate app — zero of 346 SAP goods receipts in July and August, Rs 20.6 Cr in August. Different physical gate, or the app just is not used there?

My guess
Same gate, app not used — Mart's receipts are keyed straight into SAP by their own team.
blocks: Whether any of the inbound half of this study can be extended to Mart.
20

The line-clearance checklist has never once been answered NO — 216 clearances, 1,944 checkpoint answers, not a single failure — and 21 of the 47-minute changeover is spent waiting for QA to sign it. Is QA on the floor or called across?

My guess
QA is called across rather than standing on the line, and the checklist is a formality nobody fails. I would keep the checklist and move QA closer.
blocks: Whether the scheduler should batch SKUs to dodge changeovers (worth about 12 hours of line time in August) or ignore them.
21

Nobody has ever signed a waste approval — 517 logs, four signature slots each, zero signatures since May. Is that chain meant to be used, or is it paperwork the app came with?

My guess
Dead paperwork the app shipped with. The waste logging itself is real and useful; the four signatures are not.
blocks: Whether waste percentages from this app can be quoted outside the plant.
22

Two housekeeping items nobody owns: the factory app's order feed has been failing since 17 August because it still points at the old JSAP box (103.89.45.75), and one truck, HR67C6723, has been showing as inside the plant since 22 June. Who should fix these?

My guess
IT, on both. JSAP moved to 138.252.101.118 — it is a one-line repoint. The truck is a record somebody forgot to close, not a truck.
blocks: A forward-looking view of what will need space, and trusting the inside-vehicles board as a live signal.

Source: jolly/out/QUESTIONS-FOR-DAMAN.csv. Twelve further questions arose during the study and were answered from the data rather than asked.

This is a replay, not a record. It shows what the planner would have done in August 2026, standing on each morning with no later data. The factory did not run this way.
Measured: the order book, opening stock, BOMs, line speeds, realise (May–Jul), lead times, storage ceiling, and the people. Assumed: supply arrives exactly on lead time; a 2-day invoice→truck lag; rated line speed rather than the 47% observed. WhatsApp replies are written in by the simulation, not received.
Every number traces to sim/sim-inputs.json.
